first.rationale: Onboarding completion and activation are both declining, and prior evidence indicates that shortening onboarding and reducing signup friction improved time-to-value and first-week activation. A guarded simplification experiment is more likely to improve sustainable qualified revenue than immediately matching competitor pricing, while downstream qualified activation and retention should be monitored to ensure completion gains translate into durable value.

final.rationale: Run a small guarded onboarding simplification test, prioritizing the documented completion and time-to-value gains while monitoring qualified activation, 30-day retention, and qualified revenue. The onboarding result improved retention, but the signup-specific SMB result included a 1% retention decline and did not generalize beyond SMB, so segment scope and downstream quality gates are necessary. This directly addresses both current onboarding and activation declines without sacrificing sustainable revenue for broad price cuts.
